title: Lift a rod over a row of glasses onto two rests
instruction: Lift the wooden rod over the glasses and lay it across the two wooden rests without knocking over any glass.
context: Carrying a long item such as a curtain rod, broom or shelf board past fragile things is an everyday two-handed chore: the robot has to lift high enough, keep the item level and under control, and put it down where it belongs.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A pine square dowel stained dark brown, 2.5 x 2.5 x 40 cm, 150 g, lies crosswise (parallel to the line between the bases) with its centre 14 cm forward, on the centre line. (2) Three glass tumblers, 7 cm in diameter and 10 cm tall, 250 g each, stand upright in a crosswise row 24 cm forward, their centres at 8 cm left, 0 and 8 cm right of the centre line (9 cm gaps). (3) Two pine blocks stained dark brown, 5 cm deep (front to back) x 3 cm wide x 4 cm tall, fixed to the table with their centres 34 cm forward and 16 cm left and right of the centre line. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: 1.0: the rod lies still for 3 s across both blocks (its underside within 1 cm of the blocks' tops; its centre within 2.5 cm, front to back, of the blocks' centres and within 5 cm, side to side, of the centre line; each end reaching to within 1 cm of the outer face of the block on its side or beyond) and every tumbler is upright (tilted less than 10 degrees) and less than 2 cm from where it started. 0.5: every tumbler undisturbed as above, and the rod on the table wholly beyond the far side of the row of tumblers (more than 27.5 cm forward), but not across both blocks. 0.0: any tumbler tilted 10 degrees or more or moved 2 cm or more, whatever happened to the rod, or any other outcome.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed: stand the tumblers back on their marks and put the rod back at its start. For real trials, thick-walled or polycarbonate tumblers of the same size and weight keep a knocked-over tumbler from breaking.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1 with PhysX, 20 Hz control) of a calibrated two-arm table. Simplified: the dowel is a solid box, the tumblers are solid cylinders with a glass-like colour (no transparency, breakage or contents), the blocks are fixed in place, friction and contact use the simulator's defaults, and the cameras render at 320 x 176.
